task_instance: Given a small sample C 'System Under Test' (sut_original.c: a length-prefixed, checksummed packet parser whose interesting/buggy logic in process_payload() is gated behind a near-unguessable checksum check, plus a time()-seeded PRNG in initialize()), apply the fuzzing-obstacles technique: identify both obstacles, patch them with FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION conditional compilation (sut_patched.c) following SKILL.md's documented patterns, assess false-positive risk for each patch, and write a companion libFuzzer harness reference (fuzz_harness.c).
blocker_detail: The core deliverable of this technique -- source-level patching of obstacles behind #ifdef/#ifndef FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION guards -- is pure text editing and was fully produced and verified by manual code-path tracing. SKILL.md's Step 3 ('Verify Coverage Improvement': rebuild with fuzzing instrumentation, run the fuzzer, compare llvm-cov coverage) is a secondary/optional verification step that requires a C compiler and running a fuzzer binary, which this runtime cannot do; this was noted in patch_notes.md as an unexecuted step but did not block the actual patching deliverable, so it is not recorded as the overall blocker.
evidence: Files produced in the work directory: sut_original.c (sample SUT with a checksum obstacle in parse_packet() gating process_payload(), and a time()-seeded srand() in initialize()); sut_patched.c (both obstacles patched per SKILL.md's 'Bypass Checksum Validation' and 'Deterministic PRNG Seeding' patterns: the checksum-mismatch early-return is wrapped in #ifndef FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION / #endif, and srand() is split into an #ifdef FUZZING_BUILD_MODE_UNSAFE_FOR_PRODUCTION branch with a fixed seed 12345 vs. an #else branch keeping time(NULL)); fuzz_harness.c (libFuzzer entry point calling parse_packet(), documented as reference-only since it is not compiled/run here); patch_notes.md (documents Step 1 obstacle identification, Step 2 patch diff summary, Step 4 false-positive risk assessment for each patch reasoning about process_payload()'s lack of dependence on checksum correctness and bounds-checking being unchanged, and an explicit manual trace of a sample input byte sequence AB 05 DE AD BE EF 00 <wrong-checksum> showing the original file rejects it (ERROR_INVALID_CHECKSUM, process_payload never reached) while the patched file (macro defined) falls through to process_payload and reaches the NULL-deref bug, confirming the patch has its intended effect). Verification method: manual review confirming (a) production-build behavior in sut_patched.c is byte-for-byte identical to sut_original.c when the macro is undefined, (b) #ifdef/#ifndef/#endif directives are balanced and syntactically valid C, and (c) a hand-traced sample input demonstrates the new code path (process_payload's NULL-deref branch) becomes reachable only in the fuzzing-build trace, matching the technique's stated goal. Actual compilation, execution, and llvm-cov coverage measurement (SKILL.md Step 3) were not performed since this runtime grants no code execution -- noted transparently in patch_notes.md but not treated as blocking the core patching deliverable.
